findings.label: L1
findings.text:
(authorization, docs) `docs/local-memory.md:46`: the doc says "Only `/rr-setup` opens that decision". That is false. `decision open --kind setup` can be called by the model from any session, at any time, in any task (`rr_state/dialog_cmd.py:66-68`). `command-choice-dialog.md:72` says this correctly ("the only other one the model may call").
why it matters: this is the page a human reads to learn who can turn packages mode on. It understates who can ask for it. The control itself still holds: only the human's pick of a label that visibly reads `… memory enable` grants anything.
fix direction: say that the model may open the setup decision, and that only the human's pick of the shown command enables memory.

findings.label: L2
findings.text:
(authorization, consistency) `hooks/guard/dialog.py:559-563`: `memory enable` is now a human-only verb with a dialog route, but `guarded()` and `HUMAN_VERB_RE` do not match it. So while a pick is live, a mismatched `memory enable` (for example with `--index sqlite` added) gets DECISION_PENDING and does not void the picks. `approve` gets CONSENT_MISMATCH. I challenged decision 1 and it holds for safety: state.py's `dialog_pick` binds the exact argv, the realpath of this state.py, the session, an open decision and single use. `test_enable_pick_used_once` pins that 5 argv variants and another project are each refused with exit 5 and leave the pick unspent. The gate's docstring "a human-only state.py command" is now incomplete, and R36.8's "a deviation voids consent" signal is lost for this verb. No test pins either behaviour at the gate.
why it matters: no grant is widened. An agent that strays from the pick keeps it and can retry, which `approve` does not allow.
fix direction: either add `memory\s+enable` to HUMAN_VERB_RE (with its contract fixture), or record in R36.8 and known-risks that memory enable is deliberately not voiding.

findings.label: L3
findings.text:
(personal data / committed policy) `skills/rr-setup/SKILL.md:54-55`: the "any other refusal" fallback tells the agent to hand the human `memory enable --period quarter [--index sqlite]` unconditionally. `setup.py fallback_lines` and `memory_decision` (setup.py:597-617) correctly drop `--period` once memory.json exists. Under `--options` (`--all`) on a packages project with period `month`, the SKILL text hands over a command that rewrites the committed `period` for every teammate (`memory_sync.enable`: `if period: policy["period"] = period`).
why it matters: the human runs it themselves, but the agent was told to give them a command that does more than the question asked.
fix direction: make the SKILL say `--period quarter` only when memory.json is absent, as R16 does.

findings.label: L4
findings.text:
(audit logging) `skills/ai-task/rr_state/memory_cmd.py:101-104`: an agent-run `memory enable` through a pick switches a committed, team-wide mode and writes `.git/hooks/pre-push`. Its only records are a stdout line and the git-ignored local `consent.jsonl` (`use`, by "state.py memory"). The use is mirrored into a task journal only if a task is in flight and a DIALOG_SYNC command runs later; `memory` is not in `cli.py:22`. `approve` through the dialog writes a journal line with `pick_data`. During `/rr-setup` there is usually no task, so nothing committed says who authorised the switch.
why it matters: `consent audit` still works locally, but after the fact a teammate cannot see from the repository that the agent ran it on a pick.
fix direction: record it as a known risk, or add a journal/ledger-mirrored event when there is a task.

findings.label: L5
findings.text:
(input validation, robustness) `rr_state/dialog_cmd.py:173-186` with `rr_state/labels.py:14`: the memory command label holds the project's absolute path, so a project path containing any LABEL_FORBIDDEN character (`& ; | < > $(` and the others), or a path long enough to push the label past 400 characters, fails `validate_label`. `setup_open` then refuses the whole spec with exit 6 before any write, so the runtime, survey and verify questions are lost too, and the SKILL drops to prose. This fails closed, so it is not a security issue, and no test pins it.
fix direction: when the memory label would fail, have setup.py leave memory out of the dialog (fallback line only) and still open the other three.

findings.label: I1
findings.text:
(consent binding, defence in depth) `rr_state/dialog.py:444-447`: `dialog_pick` accepts any live pick whose label parses as this state.py's argv. It does not check that the picked option's kind is `command`. Today the only model-supplied choice labels are setup's, and `check_setup_labels` (dialog_cmd.py:206-208) refuses any that `label_argv` parses or that start with python3/git/npx. That check is the only barrier between a "nothing runs" choice and a grant. It is pinned by `test_setup_spec_rejects_foreign_command`; I also confirmed that `ask` choice labels are "A — …" and the other openers' choices are fixed text.
why it matters: if that one check regresses, a choice pick would grant approve or memory enable.
fix direction: in `dialog_pick`, also require that the decision's option `n` for this pick is `kind: command`.

findings.label: I2
findings.text:
(injection) `skills/rr-setup/SKILL.md:63` with `dialog_cmd.py:131-135`: a verify value may be any printable string of up to 200 characters, as long as it appears as a backtick span of its label. The SKILL applies it as `$SETUP verify --set "<cmd>"`, so a value with `"`, `$`, `\` would break the quoting or be expanded in the agent's shell at setup time. setup.py's own candidates are fixed templates (`setup.py:118-124`) and never contain those characters. Only a hand-built spec reaches this, which the `safety.md` threat model accepts.
fix direction: either refuse `$ " \` in verify values in the opener, or have the SKILL pass the value via `shlex.quote`/stdin.

findings.label: I3
findings.text: (authorization surface) `rr_state/memory_sync.py:1048-1065`: the agent with a pick now installs an executable `.git/hooks/pre-push`. The shim it writes runs the first of several `$HOME/...` candidates and goes into the common hooks dir of all worktrees (or of a parent monorepo when `.ai/` sits in a subdirectory). The behaviour itself predates this change; only who can trigger it is new. `core.hooksPath` and a foreign hook are respected.

findings.label: L1
findings.text: bin/menu.js:100 — The lone-Esc abort misfires on a split escape sequence. `chunk.length === 1 && chunk[0] === 0x1b` treats any read that happens to hold only ESC as an abort. An arrow key (ESC `[` `B`) that TCP, ssh or tmux delivers as ESC then `[B` in two reads exits 130, so the user has to re-run. Nothing is written, so the cost is a re-run. Paste and Alt+key arrive in one chunk and are fine. `TestMenu` only types whole sequences and a lone ESC, so a split sequence is untested. Direction: wait about 50 ms after a lone ESC for the rest before aborting, or say in the header comment that this is accepted. · in_scope: yes

findings.label: L2
findings.text: bin/menu.js:82-92,104-111 — `finish` is not idempotent, and one chunk can emit several keypress events synchronously. The sequences I reasoned through (not run, per the no-scripts rule): `\r\r` in one read (pasted or type-ahead) calls `finish(0)` twice. It writes the `title: value` line and the value to stdout twice, so stdout is `propro`. `choose()` checks `items.some(it => it.value === r.stdout)`, finds no match and returns `null`. The installer then silently falls back to the typed prompt, with the TTY already restored. `\rq` calls `finish(0)` and then `finish(130)`. Stdout on a pipe is written synchronously and `process.exit(130)` runs before the callback, so the installer aborts after the user pressed Enter. A `done` guard on `state` would close both. · in_scope: yes

findings.label: L3
findings.text: tests/test_install_menu.py:~bare_path — The PATH filter drops every PATH directory that contains `claude` or `codex`. On a machine where `python3` or `git` lives in the same directory (for example `~/.local/bin`, which often holds the `claude` binary), the scratch run loses that tool. The failure would then show up as an install error, not as "no runtime". `process.execPath` keeps node itself safe. This is environment-dependent flakiness, not a vacuous pass: the replies wait for real prompts and an unseen prompt fails the test. · in_scope: yes

findings.label: I1
findings.text: bin/menu.js:56 — The reverse-video escape is emitted unconditionally. `NO_COLOR` is ignored, and the cursor stays hidden if menu.js dies from an uncaught exception, because the exit handler only restores raw mode through node's own reset. If the terminal is shorter than items+1 lines, the `\x1b[nA` redraw clamps and leaves stale rows. All three are cosmetic, outside the fixture corpus, and do not affect the verdict. · in_scope: no
